hypotheses.justification: The statement does not mention hfin; it is an argument only because of `include hp hfin`. It is used only in the proof, via `nat_card_cell_preimage_of_card_fiber` → `nat_card_cell_preimage` → `Nat.card_sigma`, which needs each fibre to be finite. The hypothesis `hd` (every fibre over a point of C has `Nat.card = d`) already gives what the proof needs. Per dimension n, we need `Nat.card (cell (p⁻¹' C) n) = d * Nat.card (cell C n)`, and `cell (p⁻¹' C) n` is definitionally `Σ i : cell C n, p⁻¹' {map n i 0}` (`cellPreimageEquiv` is `Equiv.refl`). `cell C n` is finite, from `FiniteType.finite_cell`. Case d ≠ 0: each fibre over a centre has `Nat.card = d ≠ 0`, hence is finite (`Nat.finite_of_card_ne_zero`), so `Nat.card_sigma` applies and the sum is d·#cell. Case d = 0: the right side is 0. The left side is also 0. If all fibres over the centres are empty, the sigma type is empty. Otherwise some fibre is nonempty with `Nat.card = 0`, hence infinite, so the sigma type is infinite and its `Nat.card` is 0. Either way `Nat.card = 0`. The rest of the proof (the vanishing bound `hN'`, `cwEulerChar_eq_sum_range`, `Finset.sum_congr`) never uses hfin. So the theorem remains true and provable with `omit hfin in`, replacing the call to `nat_card_cell_preimage_of_card_fiber` by this short case analysis. Deleting only hfin from this theorem is fine; the sibling lemmas that use it are not affected.
